proof_coverage.claim: Main result, quantifiers, proof dependencies and period normalization
proof_coverage.status: Checked against full text and original pages 1–2; no stronger main claim attributed to the authors
notes: Theorem A fixes a newform of weight k>=2 and critical integer 0<=j<=k-2, assumes local p-adic irreducibility, the stated local no-pole condition at s=j+1, and the Euler image condition containing SL2(O). Its conclusion is multiplication by one nonzero integral constant C independent of n and j. It is not the unscaled Mazur–Tate conjecture and it does not assert that C is a unit.

The separate residual irreducibility hypotheses in the global algebraic sections have an overbar on rho_f, confirmed on original pages 38 and 40. This was invisible in the plain extraction and is distinguished from the p-adic local (Irred) hypothesis. The Euler image hypothesis supplies the stronger global residual irreducibility needed by the final application.

The two central steps are the algebraic Fitting inclusion in Theorem 9.1.1 and the comparison/divisibility from Kato's Euler system in Theorem 12.2.2. The newvector class and integral lattice normalization link those steps.

The allowed constant absorbs fixed integral period discrepancies; uniformity in n is substantive. For a fixed weight there are only finitely many eligible j, so a fixed common integral multiple can absorb finitely many j-dependent normalizations, provided their n-independence has first been shown.
No odd-prime restriction or character-component replacement of the full cyclotomic Iwasawa algebra is stated; the prime-2 boundary is therefore assessed explicitly in FND02.

proof_coverage.claim: Period rings, divisibility and trace compatibility
proof_coverage.status: Internal algebra checked; cited foundational period-ring results retained as external inputs
notes: The perfect tilt, Witt Frobenius, T=[epsilon]-1 and t=log(1+T) conventions are consistently used. Frobenius is bijective on the tilde rings; psi is the left inverse on the ordinary cyclotomic period ring.

In Proposition 2.4.1(2), phi^(-m)x=t b_m implies x=p^m t phi^m(b_m); hence b=x/t lies in phi^m(B_max) for every m. This proves the claimed membership in the intersection defining B_rig^+, after using the cited divisibility input.
For Corollary 2.4.2, phi^(-m) preserves the tilde integral ring, and all nonnegative Frobenius iterates of T vanish under theta. Proposition 2.4.1(1) then gives the required T divisibility.
The trace relation Tr phi^(-1)=psi Tr makes (Tr(phi^n z))_n a compatible inverse system. Its index direction matches the later Iwasawa cohomology pairing.

proof_coverage.claim: Differential modules, the map iota-minus, decomposition and finite support
proof_coverage.status: Internal compatibility and quantifiers checked; deep comparison/completion statements accepted only as cited inputs
notes: The Sen derivation obeys Delta(tx)=tx+t Delta(x), so the weight shifts in the subsequent locally algebraic construction are consistent.

The i-th component of iota-minus is iota_0^- phi^(-i). Frobenius shifts components from i to i-1, and multiplication by a scalar b acts through phi^(-i)b. This explains the stabilization calculation in Section 5.
Proposition 3.3.1 uses all integer Frobenius iterates to obtain t-divisibility, exactly as required by Proposition 2.4.1(2); it does not infer divisibility from a single specialization.

Denominators phi^n(T) give zero components for i>n. Localizing instead at the factors phi^n(omega) gives the direct-sum behavior in Proposition 3.3.2; the factors at the other indices are units at a fixed differential specialization.

The bounded-above support observation in Remark 4.2.1 is compatible with finite-dimensional invertible Frobenius action: an eventually zero sequence satisfying an invertible finite recurrence is zero. No diagonalizability of Frobenius needs to be assumed for this argument.

proof_coverage.claim: Residue and de Rham pairings, dual-exponential normalization and explicit reciprocity
proof_coverage.status: Internal normalization chain checked; the underlying Colmez reciprocity theorem was not independently reproved
notes: The residue pairing uses sigma_{-1} on the first argument. The de Rham pairing is the absolute trace of the L_n-valued pairing, while the differential pairing uses the normalized trace convention in the paper.

The printed relation is <,>_dif=p^(-n)<,>_dR,n. With the two adjointness identities in the proof of Lemma 5.3.1, this gives the Colmez-normalized dual exponential equal to p^n times the standard dual exponential. The factor p^n is explicitly accounted for, rather than silently omitted.

Theorem 5.4.2 requires the denominator condition on (1-phi)z, a Gamma_n-fixed z, s>=r, and sufficiently large m. Proposition 3.3.1 then gives iota_s^-((1-phi)z)=0 for s>r; consequently iota_s^-z=iota_{s-1}^-z and all values with s>=r stabilize.

The passage from the cited reciprocity theorem to this tilde/denominator variant relies on the cited proof and period-ring pairings. This review checks the displayed stabilization and the use of its hypotheses, not a reconstruction of Colmez's analytic machinery.

proof_coverage.claim: Smooth and p-adic Kirillov models, local Birch lemma and Mellin parameters
proof_coverage.status: Core local computations checked, with FND01 separating the false unrestricted inverse statement
notes: The Borel action is delta(d) epsilon((b/d)x) phi((a/d)x). In particular P=diag(p,1) acts by phi(x)->phi(px). The lower-Borel principal-series Fourier model on page 19 is phi_f(x)=|x|_p chi_1(x) integral f(y)epsilon(-xy)dy.

For an unramified principal series with parameters alpha,beta, the newvector coefficients p^(-n)(alpha^(n+1)-beta^(n+1))/(alpha-beta) have generating series [(1-alpha p^(-s))(1-beta p^(-s))]^(-1). At alpha=beta this has the removable limit (n+1)(alpha/p)^n; equality of the Satake parameters is not in itself an error or a violation of the no-pole condition.

In Lemma 6.3.1 it is the function phi*chi in the twisted representation that is summed. At a unit x, the primitive Gauss sum is tau(chi)chi(x)^(-1), which cancels the chi(x) factor. At positive valuation the primitive sum vanishes, and at negative valuation the original newvector vanishes. This proves the p-deprived output, including the case where ramified twisting happens to remove some automorphic ramification.

The last paragraph on page 20 explicitly warns that the p-deprived newvector need not be the primitive newvector after cancellation of ramification. Consequently the later statement that a ramified Dirichlet-twisted L-series has trivial p-factor must be read for the Dirichlet coefficient series used in the paper, not for an incorrectly substituted primitive automorphic twist.

The Galois-twisted Gamma action on p-adic Kirillov functions is distinct from the regular variable action. Values at p^r determine a twisted-invariant function. The refined Mellin sum is interpreted by rational continuation of the tail, not as an unconditionally convergent numerical series.

For a pure tensor v tensor e1^(k-2-j)e2^j in the det^ell twist, formula (9) gives j!(tx)^(k-2+ell-j)phi_v(x). Thus a=k-2+ell-j and the possible inverse denominator is 1-p^a gamma. The no-pole evaluation s=1-a equals j+3-ell-k as printed. For ell=2-k this specializes to a=-j and s=1+j.

proof_coverage.claim: Restricted inverse needed by the actual newvector construction
proof_coverage.status: A precise local restriction repairs the inverse step for the newvector tails; the unrestricted proposition remains false
notes: The counterexample in FND01 is not a counterexample to the actual translated newvector d_n,j. For sufficiently small x, epsilon(x)=1 and the regular-unit type of K_{d_n,j} is x^(-j) times an unramified radial newvector tail.

That radial tail belongs to a finite-dimensional shift-stable space whose eigenvalues are alpha_i/p^(j+1), where alpha_i are the nontrivial local Euler parameters. The stated no-pole condition excludes eigenvalue 1 on this space. If the p-factor is 1, the tail is eventually zero.

Therefore 1-P is invertible on this specified tail space. Repeated roots are handled by the inverse of a finite Jordan block: for A=rI+N and N^d=0, (I-A)^(-1)=sum_{h=0}^{d-1} N^h/(1-r)^(h+1), provided r!=1. The simple exponential formula printed in Section 6 is insufficient by itself for repeated roots, but the finite-dimensional repair is direct.

Choose this inverse germ near zero and extend it to the outer annuli recursively by xi(x)=phi(x)+xi(px). The original support is bounded away from infinity, so after passing beyond it the solution is constant under radial p-shift. Compactly supported changes belong to the Kirillov model. The selected germ excludes the ramified homogeneous solution in FND01.

Gamma_n weight -j of d_n,j, and then the +j cyclotomic twist, are compatible with this construction because the operator commutes with the relevant action and the selected tail space is stable. This establishes the scope of a local correction; it is not a claim that every analytic comparison and generalized-model lifting in Section 7 has been independently reconstructed.

The page-25 pure-tensor input explicitly contains j!. Its displayed special-case inverse omits that common scalar. The repaired instruction is to apply (1-P)^(-1) to the complete K_z, retaining j!; the actual supercuspidal and twisted-pairing formulas later on pages 30–32 already retain it. This belongs to the same local inverse correction, not a separate issue group.

proof_coverage.claim: p-adic local Langlands and construction of local cohomology classes
proof_coverage.status: Tensor weights, finite differences and duality logic checked; cited local Langlands/lifting results remain external
notes: The identity (Sym^(k-2))^*=Sym^(k-2) tensor det^(2-k) gives the determinant twist used in Section 7. The two Kirillov models are normalized to agree by one scalar, using the cited comparison theorem.

In Lemma 7.3.1 the unipotent translation e2->p^n e1+e2 lowers the e2-degree after subtraction. Applying it j+1 times kills the degree-j vector; this gives the precise denominator power phi^n(T)^(j+1).

For diag(a,1), the monomial factor a^(k-2-j) and determinant factor a^(2-k) multiply to a^(-j). Twisting by the j-th cyclotomic character removes this Gamma_n weight, as required by the reciprocity law.

The formula pairing d_n,j^(j) against z' factors through the finite-level dual exponential. Rational Iwasawa-to-finite-level surjectivity is explicitly invoked. Local Tate duality then gives a unique rational cohomology class with the prescribed pairing.

Annihilating ker(exp*)=H_g gives c_n,j in H_e by orthogonality. H_e is contained in H_f, so the needed membership does not require a stronger equality to be independently assumed. The printed equality H_e=H_f under the no-pole hypothesis is cited to Bloch–Kato; its behavior after every ramified base change was not independently rederived here.

The supercuspidal example on page 30 has K_d(p^r)=j! p^(nj)epsilon(p^(-n))t^(-j) only at r=-n, and its inverse has that same value at r<=-n. This directly checks the support direction and the factorial in the actual class construction.

proof_coverage.claim: Twisted pairing sums and Gauss factors
proof_coverage.status: Finite character manipulations and trace normalization checked
notes: In Proposition 7.4.1 the factor p^n from reciprocity cancels the p^(-n) normalization of the differential pairing when it is replaced by the absolute de Rham trace. The latter trace is then the sum over the finite Galois group.
The change of variables in the double sum gives chi(-b), equivalently chi(-1)chi(b), on the dual-exponential side. This accounts for the chi(-1) in the analytic interpolation formula.

Applying the local Birch sum to the unmodified v_new introduces an angular chi(x) factor in a literal smooth Kirillov-function identity. The displayed page-32 intermediate identity suppresses it, but its subsequent refined Mellin evaluation uses x=p^r and the unramified extension chi(p)=1, so the evaluated coefficient j!p^(nj)tau(chi^(-1)) is unchanged. No false conclusion is inferred from this intermediate abbreviation.
The n=0 formula keeps the local Mellin/Euler factor, unlike a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character. This distinction is retained in the final Kato comparison.

proof_coverage.claim: Three-term relation and the explicit crystalline check
proof_coverage.status: Matrix identity, exceptional base layer, and displayed crystalline formula checked
notes: For n>=1 the corestriction sums diag(1+i p^n,1), i=0,...,p-1. The printed matrix factorization converts this into the Hecke sum on v_new, producing a c_n,j - delta res(c_(n-1),j). The tensor twist has already been cancelled by passing to d^(j).
At n=0 the sum runs over i=1,...,p-1. The omitted i=0 Hecke term gives the additional -1, so cor(c_1,j)=(a-delta-1)c_0,j. The base layer is not silently treated as an extension of degree p.

For the explicit crystalline subsection, alpha!=beta and alpha,beta!=p are stated hypotheses. Thus all denominators alpha/p-beta/p, 1-alpha/p and 1-beta/p occurring in Proposition 7.6.1 are nonzero within that subsection.

Writing omega=e_(alpha/p)-e_(beta/p), the projection of k_n onto the common de Rham quotient e is exactly the finite epsilon-weighted geometric sum plus the two tail fractions on page 35. Dividing by alpha/p-beta/p gives iota_n^-(w_n), so the exponential formula agrees with the pairing definition.

Remark 7.6.2 explicitly says the crystalline formula alone does not establish the uniform integrality later needed. The report must not attribute such an integral conclusion to this rational computation.

proof_coverage.claim: Integral local classes and torsion in cohomology
proof_coverage.status: The lattice-duality argument was reconstructed; printed coefficient-module formulas need the conventional reading described below
notes: The target of the asserted integrality is the image of H^1(K_n,T(1+j)) in rational cohomology, or equivalently the torsion-free quotient, not an injection of the entire integral group. This distinction is made explicitly by the authors.

The exact-annihilator lemma follows from integral local duality and reduction modulo varpi: the quotient of H^1(T^*)/varpi in H^1(T^*/varpi) is H^2(T^*)[varpi], dual to H^0(A_1)/varpi with A_1=V(1+j)/T(1+j). The image of integral torsion on the opposite side has the same dimension, giving W1=W2-perp.

More precisely, H^1(T_1)_tors=H^0(A_1)/image H^0(V_1); in the irreducible nontrivial-Hodge-weight setting H^0(V_1)=0. These are the correct discrete-module identities for the proof. The displayed H^0(T_1) and tensor placement on page 37 should not be read as a valid general replacement for H^0(A_1).

Conditional on the key integral pairing furnished by the chosen integral local-Langlands normalization, the minimal-r argument in Proposition 7.7.2 is correct: a hypothetical varpi^r c with r>0 reduces into W1, hence equals torsion+varpi h', lowering r. The occurrences of p where that argument uses the uniformizer are local notation slips, not an independent counterexample to the lattice conclusion.

The integral local-Langlands normalization itself and its compatibility with all integral finite-level pairings were not rederived from the Banach representation construction; this remains an explicitly identified deep input.

proof_coverage.claim: Selmer groups, control and reflexive-hull construction
proof_coverage.status: Definitions and finite-level map logic checked; arithmetic input retained as cited
notes: The finite-level Selmer condition is unramified away from p with the Bloch–Kato condition at p. At infinite level the p-condition is removed using the cited universal-norm theorem under local irreducibility.

Proposition 8.2.1 includes both (Irred) and residual global irreducibility. Its finite bounded error B_n is not asserted to vanish. After duality, the map from the local integral finite group and B_n-dual surjects onto the control obstruction exactly as needed.

Theorem 8.2.2 obtains rank-one Iwasawa cohomology from Kato and rank-one infinite-level Selmer dual by subtracting only Lambda-torsion local terms. These are arithmetic theorems, not results numerically verified here.

For odd p, the full Iwasawa algebra is a finite product of two-dimensional regular power-series rings after character decomposition, and a rank-one reflexive module is free componentwise. This explains the reflexive-hull identification and finite-index ideal used in Sections 8–9. At p=2 that regular-ring reasoning is not justified by the stated algebra; see FND02.
The restriction-transfer compatibility in Lemma 8.2.3 has the expected direction: restriction of a local class maps to the transfer nu_m^n of its lower-level theta coefficient.

proof_coverage.status: The algebraic proof is checked in its regular odd-prime setting; the prime-2 counterexample is separated in FND02
notes: The directions in Lemma 9.2.1 are correct: a quotient increases the zeroth Fitting ideal; a short exact sequence gives a product contained in the middle Fitting ideal; base change gives the Fitting ideal of coinvariants.

In Lemma 9.2.3, reducing to a principal ideal fLambda is legitimate. On a nonzero component, A/fLambda embeds in Lambda/fLambda, which has no nonzero finite submodule over the two-dimensional regular ring. Localizing at height-one primes identifies it with Lambda/fLambda because Lambda/A is finite. This yields the same principal characteristic/Fitting ideal. The zero generator is trivial and zero components are handled separately.
Lemma 9.2.4 correctly applies the preceding result to the inverse image of I_n under A->A_Gamma_n and then uses Fitting base change.

For Theorem 9.1.1, the torsion-free quotient has no Gamma_n-invariants in the regular odd-prime setting, giving the stated exact coinvariant sequence. Quotienting by the image E_n of the local classes produces the short exact sequence used in the Fitting product estimate.

The bounded finite group B_n is harmless in this estimate because the actual finite Selmer dual is a quotient of the middle module. The use of Greenberg to exclude finite submodules of X_tor is specifically identified; it is not replaced by an assumption that B_n=0.
The transition from Fitt(X_tor) to char(X_tor) on page 42 is the exact place where the false prime-2 version of Lemma 9.2.2 would be needed.

proof_coverage.claim: Mazur–Tate normalization, local no-pole boundary and functional-equation caveat
proof_coverage.status: Boundary algebra checked; the internal interpolation normalization mismatch is FND03
notes: The explicit sign-projector definitions on page 42 do not algebraically yield the displayed interpolation formula (18); the finite Fourier calculation and a precise local correction are given in FND03.

Remark 10.1.3 correctly cautions that its functional-equation multiplier need not be integral at small n; one must not assert an integral equivalence of the two Selmer/Fitting conjectures in every layer merely from that functional equation.
For p not dividing N, a pole at j+1 means p^(j+1) is one of the two Euler roots. Its complex absolute value p^((k-1)/2) forces j=(k-3)/2 and then a_p=p^((k-1)/2)(1+psi(p)).

For p||N and unramified nebentype, a_p^2=psi(p)p^(k-2); requiring a_p=p^(j+1) gives j=(k-4)/2, psi(p)=1 and the positive sign for a_p. The exact-nebentype-conductor case similarly gives j=(k-3)/2. These alternatives retain the critical integer constraint, so for example the displayed negative or half-integral j values at small weight produce no eligible critical j.
The original text imposes no unverified exceptional-zero correction when the no-pole hypothesis fails; it explicitly leaves that case outside the theorem.

proof_coverage.claim: Kato interpolation, primitive characters and recurrence propagation
proof_coverage.status: Local-to-global algebra checked subject to the period corrections and explicitly noted normalization limitation
notes: The Kato interpolation theorem is used with the p-factor removed, and the n=0 refined Mellin factor restores precisely that factor. At a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character the coefficient L-series is already p-deprived, consistently with the discussion on page 20.

The character sum in Proposition 10.2.3 has sigma^(-1); evaluating it gives chi^(-1) in the local pairing and then chi(-1) in Proposition 7.4.1. The t^(-j) and t^j factors cancel in the de Rham pairing.

Under corestriction compatibility of z_K, summing the lifts of sigma gives pairing of cor(c_(n+1)) with z_(K,n). The local recurrence then gives the global coefficient psi(p)p^(k-2) and the transfer nu_(n-1)^n. The n=0 recurrence is checked separately.

Once character values for primitive characters and the lower-level projection agree, induction in n determines all character values in L[G_n]; the integral group algebra embeds there. This justifies the method of recovering equality from primitive interpolation plus recurrence.

The printed proof produces sign-dependent ratios <e,omega_f> Omega_f^+/Omega_f,K^+ and <e,omega_f> Omega_f^-/Omega_f,K^-. The compatible choice making them a single scalar is not reconstructed in this review; see the normalization clarification in unresolved_questions. This is not classified as a proved additional defect.

proof_coverage.claim: Comparison of the two algebraic theta constructions and the involution
proof_coverage.status: Formal duality and coefficient chase checked; coefficient-ring conventions and cited arithmetic duality retained as limitations
notes: The torsion local quotient W is killed by Hom_Lambda(-,Lambda), so Hom of the full cohomology dual and Hom of the Selmer dual agree. This explains the same reflexive hull for the two constructions.

The residual representation overbar is visible in the invariant-vanishing statement on page 47. The argument belongs to the residual-irreducible global setting of Section 11, not to an unsupported assertion that p-adic irreducibility alone always kills integral invariants.
The coefficient chase gives b_sigma=<c,res(w_n^sigma)>=<c^(sigma^-1),res(w_n)>; changing sigma to sigma^-1 produces exactly the involution in Theorem 11.2.3.

For a nontrivial coefficient extension O_L/Z_p, the displayed Z_p-valued Pontryagin dual formulas on pages 47–48 require a compatible coefficient trace/dual-lattice convention, or equivalently an O_L-linear dual into L/O_L. The underlying coefficient-wise group-ring pairing explains the involution, but this review does not claim that the printed Z/p^n target by itself is a fully specified O_L-perfect pairing.

The pseudo-isomorphism and characteristic-ideal identity involving the Selmer complex in Theorem 12.1.2 are explicitly external duality input. The subsequent use of its stated involution is internally consistent.

proof_coverage.claim: Final Euler-system divisibility, zero divisors and integral constant
proof_coverage.status: Formal final deduction checked without cancelling a possible finite-level zero divisor
notes: Write F=char_Lambda H_P^2 and alpha=F*b in Lambda, as supplied by the one-sided Euler-system divisibility. Set P_n=sum <c_n^sigma,res(w_n)> sigma.

Then iota(theta_alg)=F_n P_n. Lemma 12.2.1 gives D iota(theta_an)=alpha_n P_n=b_n F_n P_n=b_n iota(theta_alg). This obtains the required finite-level identity directly. It does not cancel F_n in Lambda_n, where F_n may be a zero divisor or may vanish at a character.

The scalar-linearity lemma follows for a group element tau from <c^sigma,tau w>=<c^(tau^-1 sigma),w>, followed by the variable substitution in the group-ring sum. Linearity and continuity give the Lambda statement.

If the compatible comparison scalar D lies in O_L, take C=D. Otherwise D^(-1) lies in O_L because O_L is a valuation ring, giving theta_an=D^(-1)b theta_alg and C=1. This last step is correct for a genuinely scalar nonzero D.

Neither the cited Kato main-conjecture divisibility nor the Selmer-complex duality theorem was re-proved. Their precise applicability at prime 2 is part of the boundary limitation rather than silently certified.
